title: hotpage-clustered-slots-allocator: clustered slot allocation with eviction-feedback for hot KV pages
author: Ira Chen
description:
Context and motivation: Hot KV pages emit a high fraction of requests that dominate latency tail under contention. Existing slab/slot allocators favored global fragmentation reduction but did not encode temporal locality strongly enough for the hotpage common-case, which led to suboptimal cache retention and increased KV cache churn during continuous batching and high-concurrency schedules. This PR introduces a clustered slot allocator and an eviction-feedback controller that bias retention toward recently active 'hotpage clusters' and surfaces lightweight eviction signals to the scheduler and batching layer.

Summary of changes: Introduces ClusteredSlotAllocator (new allocator strategy) with a hotpage cluster table, per-cluster soft-reservation tokens, and an LRU-like micro-evictor that prefers cold clusters. Adds EvictionFeedbackController that samples eviction counters and emits feedback events consumed by the scheduler's FeedbackBridge to adjust work-stealing and batch sizing. Kernel/hint integration: allocator exposes per-page 'stability' hints that compilation/kernel-selection code can use to choose between streaming-friendly kernels vs caching-optimized kernels. Continuous batching synergy: feedback path signals when prefetched KV prefixes are stable so batching can be slightly more aggressive without hurting p95 latency.

Highlights and measurable impact: - p50 stable, p95 latency improved 8–12% across two internal microbench workloads (hotprefix-heavy and mixed-read-write) with the new allocator and feedback loop enabled. - End-to-end throughput improved 6–10% on the hotprefix workload due to reduced KV cache churn and fewer cold misses. - Unit-token cost reduction in synthetic billing sim: ~4% for steady-state hot workloads.

Compatibility and rollout: Default is behind a runtime feature-flag (env var and Console toggle). Migration is non-breaking: allocator can run alongside the legacy slab allocator per pool and be selected by policy for specific model routes. The feedback channel is best-effort and degrades gracefully when disabled.

Testing and validation: comprehensive unit tests for allocator invariants, integration tests that exercise feedback->scheduler interactions, and perf canary runs in perf-canary cluster. Bench harness scripts added under src/runtime/benchmarks and a Console doc describing configuration and expected metrics.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-2484) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Bench and canary runs performed - [x] Feature-flagged rollout path documented

Related work: complements earlier KV allocator and pinning improvements by focusing on cluster-level locality and active eviction signals.

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps eviction feedback rate-limited and uses jittered sampling to avoid adding load; further tuning will be done via console metrics and canary telemetry.
